open_release.rationale: The sources stress reproducible code and documentation, not releasing simulated data in place of real data.

pipeline_testing.rationale: Simulated data are said to be used to test and validate analysis methods, but a realism claim is also made, so it is unclear this counts as pipeline testing.

quotes.text: Many methods have been tested, developed, and validated using simulated datasets.

ml_augmentation.rationale: No machine-learning or augmentation framing appears.

statistical_replication.rationale: Splatter estimates parameters from real data and provides functions and figures comparing simulations with real datasets.

quotes.text: Splatter also has functions for comparing simulations and real datasets.
Unfortunately, current simulations are often poorly documented, their similarity to real data is not demonstrated, or reproducible code is not available.

causal_inference.rationale: No causal or structural-model framing appears.

education.rationale: The README points to a vignette for getting started, but no teaching or course use is shown.

benchmarking.rationale: The paper provides a framework for comparing simulation models and positions simulations as a known truth for evaluating analysis methods.
